findings.title: Exclusive cache lock is held during manifest I/O and is not followed by a cache recheck
findings.body: After a caller observes an empty cache, it acquires the write lock and holds it while reading/parsing the manifest (and potentially performing CDN I/O if enabled). Other concurrent cold-cache callers have already passed the initial read check, so when each eventually acquires the lock it does not recheck the cache and performs another serialized manifest load. A burst of initial requests therefore causes N sequential reads rather than one load (or concurrent loads), and in development every request is serialized behind filesystem I/O. Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock, or perform I/O outside the cache lock and lock only when publishing the result.
